verification.reason: core.md:413 says a later report "is taken only when none is stored, when it is the stored report again... or when its verdict is stronger", and that it "replaces the stored report whole". The code does more than that. `refusal()` (verification.ts:145-150) returns undefined for a weaker or equal report that answers `different` where the stored report did not. `after()` then keeps the stored report and merges only the `different` answers (`withDifferent`, lines 166-169). `whole()` also merges stored `different` answers into a stronger report (line 132). So the doc omits the `different`-wins exception that the cited decision (line 12) and the code both implement. The doc is wrong about when a later report is taken and what the stored record becomes. The scenario in the finding traces correctly through the code.

Traced the replay. The first call stores a report whose verdict is not stronger, but which answers `different` for a finding the record lacks. `after` merges that answer into the stored record, and `whole` is false. On replay, `whole(report)` is still false: the reasons differ, and the verdict is not stronger. `refusal` then finds `stored.matches[id] === "different"`, so the `some` check fails and it returns the "already judged" string. `upsertVerification` throws at line 1072, and `failed(...)` turns that into an error result. The head's comment says a replay finds its own report stored, but this path is not covered. `report_verdict` is `replay: "safe"`, so it can be re-executed after a crash. The base returned early when `previous` equalled `after(verification)`, so it didn't refuse this replay. The record stays correct and only the replayed result is wrong. The trigger needs a crash between the tool's commit and its result commit.

Reports are judged per claim. A claim's first report stands, with its reason and any lowering, and a later report of it is refused unless its verdict is stronger; a stronger verdict replaces the first whole. A sameness answer of `different` from any report wins, so a later report at an equal verdict may still turn `same` into `different`, and nothing turns it back. A lowering with no evidence at the head is refused before anything is stored. [The decision](decisions/2026-11-28-a-claims-first-report-stands.md) says why. The merged defect takes the highest severity among its claims after lowering.

Choice:

1. `report_verdict` refuses a second report of a claim unless its verdict is stronger than the stored one. A replay of the stored report is taken. Otherwise the first report stands: its reason, its evidence, its sameness answers and its lowering. A stronger later verdict still replaces the first report, its lowering included, as before. The refusal says which verdict is stored and any lowering it holds.
2. A sameness answer of `different`, from any report of the claim, wins over `same`, so an answer may move from same to different and never back. A later report at an equal or weaker verdict that answers `different` where the stored report did not is taken for that answer alone, and the tool says so; the rest of the first report stands. A stronger report that answers `same` where a stored report answered `different` keeps `different`. The maintainer ruled this on 2026-11-28, in the coordinator's session ("A"), on the round's finding that a first `same` could not be taken back.
3. `report_verdict` refuses a lowering with no evidence location at the head before anything is stored, and says that nothing was recorded, so the verifier can send the report again with evidence, or without the lowering.

That is more than one step, a P0, or a result that is `nit` or that the table in force resolves `silent`. It is also an injection attempt, a deterministic co-report, or a `refuted` verdict. A refused lowering still records the verdict.
A lowering the fence refuses still records the verdict, and `report_verdict` says why in its result. A lowering with no evidence at the head records nothing, as the per-claim rule below says.
